step1_analysis.circuit_type: CML (Current Mode Logic) Data Buffer / Amplifier
step1_analysis.description: A two-stage differential CML buffer with emitter-follower inputs and outputs. It is designed for high-speed serial communication (up to 50 Gb/s) and uses a standard ECL/CML topology with a -3.6V negative supply.

paper_reference.title: 50-Gb/s SiGe BiCMOS 4 : 1 Multiplexer and 1 : 4 Demultiplexer for Serial Communication Systems

sky130_expected.calculation: V_swing = I_tail * R_load. Assuming a tail current of 6mA and R_load = 50 ohms, V_swing = 6mA * 50 = 300mV.
sky130_expected.reasoning: CML logic swing is determined by the tail current and load resistor. 300mV is standard for high-speed CML to keep transistors out of deep saturation while providing enough noise margin.

dc_gain.description: Low-frequency voltage gain of the buffer.

sky130_expected.calculation: Gain = gm * R_load. For a buffer, the gain is typically designed to be around 0 dB (unity) to restore logic levels without excessive amplification.
sky130_expected.reasoning: As a digital buffer, it restores the 300mV swing. The small-signal gain is typically near unity.

sky130_expected.calculation: f_3dB ≈ 1 / (2 * pi * R_load * C_out). With R_load = 50 ohms and estimated SKY130 NMOS parasitic capacitance C_out ≈ 100fF, f_3dB ≈ 31.8 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: To support 50 Gb/s, the analog bandwidth must be at least half the baud rate (25 GHz). SKY130 NMOS can achieve this with small device sizing and 50-ohm loads.

power_dissipation.description: Total DC power consumed by the buffer.

paper_reported.value: 1.47 W (410 mA at 3.6V for entire MUX)

sky130_expected.calculation: Power = VDD * I_total. The circuit has 8 current branches. If each is biased at 6mA, I_total = 48mA. Power = 1.8V * 48mA = 86.4mW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Mapped to a 1.8V SKY130 supply, the power dissipation is significantly lower than the 3.6V ECL implementation, though the current remains similar to maintain the 300mV swing across 50 ohms.

propagation_delay.description: Time delay from the input crossing 50% to the output crossing 50%.

sky130_expected.calculation: t_d ≈ 0.69 * R_load * C_out per stage. 0.69 * 50 * 100fF = 3.45ps. For two stages, total delay ≈ 7ps.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The delay is dominated by the RC time constant of the load resistors and the parasitic capacitances of the transistors.

rise_fall_time.description: 20% to 80% transition time of the output signal.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Rise and fall times are limited by the bandwidth of the output stage. 11ps is sufficient for a 20ps unit interval (50 Gb/s).

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC power, AC bandwidth/gain, and transient swing, delay, and rise/fall times of the CML buffer.
step3_testbench.spice:
* 50-Gb/s CML Buffer Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

* Define a high-speed NPN model to simulate the extracted Q instances
.model npn npn (is=1e-16 bf=100 tf=2p cje=20f cjc=20f)

* Power Supplies (ECL levels)
V_GND GND 0 DC 0
V_VEE -3.6V 0 DC -3.6

* Bias and Reference
VVB VB 0 DC -2.5
VREF REF 0 DC -0.15

* Input Signal (50 Gb/s -> 25 GHz fundamental)
VIN IN 0 DC -0.15 AC 1 SIN(-0.15 0.15 25G)

* --- DUT Netlist ---
Q1 N8 N6 N3 npn
Q2 GND REF N5 npn
R1 N16 GND 50
R2 N17 -3.6V 50
R3 N15 -3.6V 50
Q3 N1 N5 N11 npn
R4 N1 GND 50
R5 N8 GND 50
R6 N20 -3.6V 50
R7 N10 -3.6V 50
R8 N9 -3.6V 50
Q4 GND N1 N7 npn
Q5 N16 N7 N3 npn
R9 REF GND 50
Q6 N0 N12 N11 npn
R10 N19 -3.6V 50
Q7 GND N16 OUT2 npn
R11 IN GND 50
R12 N0 GND 50
Q8 GND N8 OUT1 npn
Q9 GND N0 N6 npn
R13 N14 -3.6V 50
R14 N28 -3.6V 50
Q10 N7 VB N17 npn
Q11 N11 VB N20 npn
Q12 OUT1 VB N9 npn
Q13 OUT2 VB N10 npn
Q14 N3 VB N14 npn
Q15 N6 VB N28 npn
Q16 GND IN N12 npn
Q17 N5 VB N15 npn
Q18 N12 VB N19 npn
* -------------------

.control
* 1. DC Operating Point & Power
op
let power = -i(V_VEE) * 3.6
print power

* 2. AC Analysis for Bandwidth and Gain
ac dec 50 100M 100G
let gain_db = vdb(OUT1)
meas ac dc_gain find gain_db at=100M
let gain_3db = dc_gain - 3
meas ac bw_3db when gain_db=$&gain_3db fall=1

* 3. Transient Analysis for Swing, Delay, Rise/Fall Time
tran 1p 200p
* Measure over a stable window to avoid startup transients
meas tran v_max max v(OUT1) from=100p to=200p
meas tran v_min min v(OUT1) from=100p to=200p
let v_swing = v_max - v_min
print v_swing

let v_20 = v_min + 0.2 * v_swing
let v_80 = v_min + 0.8 * v_swing
let v_mid = v_min + 0.5 * v_swing

* Measure on the 3rd cycle to ensure steady state
meas tran t_rise trig v(OUT1) val=$&v_20 rise=3 targ v(OUT1) val=$&v_80 rise=3
meas tran t_fall trig v(OUT1) val=$&v_80 fall=3 targ v(OUT1) val=$&v_20 fall=3

* Delay from IN to OUT1
meas tran t_delay trig v(IN) val=-0.15 rise=3 targ v(OUT1) val=$&v_mid rise=3

quit
.endc
.end
